notes: Round 51 lane NAMES: the hand-written design (families, habitats, tiers, names). build.py expands it over the zones' belts and the water survey into draft.json and the preview page. Edit this file, then rerun build.py.

shore.label: Sea shore
shore.text: Sea water up to about 16 nodes from dry land (or about 6-8 nodes deep) and the beach above it. Only mobs that follow a player ashore live here.

belt.label: Shelf and belt
belt.text: Sea water farther out inside the zone: the shelf, the wider coastal belt and the bay rims. It belongs to the zone on land (level, faction, PvP). Pure swimmers live here.

bay_deep.label: Deep bay middle
bay_deep.text: The deep middle of a bay; it may be deadly for new players.

channel.label: Dragon channel
channel.text: The shallow organic channels to the dragon islands; they take their island's mob level.

open_sea.label: Open sea
open_sea.text: Beyond the belt. Elites only here.

freshwater.label: Lakes and rivers
freshwater.text: Lakes, rivers and swamp pools (swamp pools count as lake in the water query, round plan T2).

cave_water.label: Cave water
cave_water.text: Pools in caves. No family proposed.

tier_note: Drop tier = floor((level - 1) / 10) + 1. T3 starts at 20 so a capital's L20-23 belt takes the T3 name (it counts as T3, naming rule 4); T2 ends at 20 so an L18-20 belt takes the T2 name.

families.label: Tortoise
families.behaviour_text: Neutral beast: bites back when attacked, normal XP and loot.

source.facts: type animal, not passive, has a punch animation (frames from 300), walk speed 0.2

families.why: Ruling S15 names it: the neutral water beast on shores and at lakes, at zone level. Slow, so a player can always walk away.

families.label: Frog
families.from_level_why: No hostile frogs in the L1-2 home belts (the user took the NAMES lane's question 5 as recommended, 2026-10-19); the tortoise stays there.
families.behaviour_text: Hostile amphibian: hops after a player through water and onto the bank.

source.facts: type animal, passive in the source, walks and swims (fly_in water); no punch animation, so the port bites with its walk frames (an open question for the user)

families.why: The one hostile family for lakes, rivers and swamp pools in every zone: today the banks hold only land mobs, and the crocodile only three swamp zones.

families.label: Stingray
families.from_level_why: No hostile water mob in the L1-2 home belts, as for the frog (Round 51 MOBS M2); the survey found no stingray water there anyway.
families.behaviour_text: Hostile pure swimmer: glides over the seabed; resets and swims off when its target leaves the water (S11).

source.facts: type monster, dogfight attack, swims (fly), has a punch animation (frames from 200)

families.why: The one hostile family of the shelf, the coastal belt, the bay rims and the channels, at zone level (channels: island level). It keeps away from the bank (S10), so nobody fights it from land.

families.label: Shark
families.behaviour_text: Hostile pure swimmer with fixed levels: the Bay Shark in the deep bay middles, the Abyssal Shark (scaled about 2.5 times, a seldom spawn) in the open sea.

source.facts: type monster, dogfight attack, swims (fly), has a punch animation (frames from 100)

families.why: Rulings S12 and S13 name both: the Bay Shark (fixed L30, normal) and the Abyssal Shark (elite, open sea, next to the Kraken). World slots: one name, one level everywhere (contract item 3).

families.label: Goby
families.behaviour_text: Critter fish: swims anywhere in sea water for atmosphere, flees, drops fish (S14). Never a kill target.
families.why: The sea's one critter fish, as the Reed Angelfish is the lakes'. Same API as our mobs (mobs_redo), MIT, so a cheap port.

families.label: Crab
families.behaviour_text: Shown as it is: the shore ladder, neutral and hostile sub-types by level band, on sandy sea shore.

source.facts: the pattern the new families follow (sea plan section 5)

families.why: Stays (brief). The quest-ready pattern: one family, sub-types by level band, a shore kind of each zone recipe, names per slot.

families.label: Crocodile
families.behaviour_text: Shown as it is: ambushes on swamp banks and shores of three troll and undead zones.

families.label: Reed Angelfish
families.behaviour_text: Shown as it is: the lakes' critter fish, one Raw Fish per kill.

source.facts: independent water spawn authority, world slot L1

families.label: Kraken
families.behaviour_text: Shown as it is: the open-sea guard, fixed L70 elite.

source.facts: independent water spawn authority in deep-ocean columns, world slot L70

world_slots.name: Bay Shark
world_slots.why: S12: a fixed level 30, normal tier, in the deep middle of the four bays.

world_slots.name: Abyssal Shark
world_slots.why: S13: an elite shark scaled two to three times, a seldom spawn in the open sea next to the Kraken. Level 70 like the Kraken, so the open sea has one level (an open question for the user).

world_slots.name: Tide Goby
world_slots.why: S10, S14: the sea's critter fish, anywhere in sea water, fish loot.

left_out.label: Otter
left_out.why: Frog and tortoise already cover the banks; a third bank family would make water a second land (S18). First reserve if the banks feel thin.

left_out.label: Beaver
left_out.source: reference_projects/animalworld/beaver.lua (MIT); type monster, has a punch animation
left_out.why: Overlaps the frog. The alternative to the frog if a bite animation matters (an open question for the user).

left_out.label: Hermit crab
left_out.why: The crab ladder already holds the start-zone shores (L3-10).

left_out.label: Lobster
left_out.why: A seabed walker next to the crab and the stingray; one family too many for the shelf.

left_out.label: Manatee
left_out.why: The tortoise is the neutral water beast. Reserve for the kelp belt if the belt feels empty.

left_out.label: Squid (small Kraken)
left_out.source: the vendored Kraken mesh at a small scale (mods/ENTITIES/grug_mobs/models/grug_mobs_kraken.b3d); also reference_projects/animalworld/squid.lua (MIT)
left_out.why: The cheapest second belt family (no port), but a small Kraken would blur the Kraken's look. Reserve.

left_out.label: Tropical fish (VoxeLibre)
left_out.source: reference_projects/VoxeLibre/mods/ENTITIES/mobs_mc/tropical_fish.lua, models extra_mobs_tropical_fish_a/b.b3d (GPL-3.0 models, CC BY-SA textures)
left_out.why: The goby is the sea's one critter fish; a VoxeLibre port also brings share-alike media.

left_out.label: Salmon (VoxeLibre)
left_out.why: Critter role taken by the goby and the Reed Angelfish.

left_out.label: Cod schools (VoxeLibre)
left_out.why: Critter role taken by the goby; schools cost objects.

left_out.label: Dolphin groups (VoxeLibre)
left_out.why: Groups cost objects and a group behaviour we do not have; not needed for levels.

left_out.label: Glow squid (VoxeLibre)
left_out.why: Atmosphere only, where nobody swims; later if wanted.

left_out.label: Carp
left_out.why: The Reed Angelfish already is the lakes' critter fish.

left_out.label: Trout
left_out.why: As carp.

left_out.label: Nymph
left_out.why: Atmosphere only; the lakes have the Reed Angelfish.

left_out.label: Diving beetle
left_out.why: As nymph.

left_out.label: Hippo
left_out.why: The crocodile already holds the swamp and jungle waters.

left_out.label: Seahorse
left_out.why: The goby is the sea's one critter fish.

left_out.label: Olm
left_out.why: Cave pools are rare and no ruling asks for them; atmosphere only.

left_out.label: Seal
left_out.why: Out of scope (S16).

left_out.label: Sea turtle
left_out.why: Out of scope (S15): a later art job.
